# Bookself

> Bookself is open-source, Git-native publishing software for books, papers, course texts, and other long-form work. It keeps manuscripts as plain Markdown files, uses Git history for revision and review, separates private work-in-progress from public releases, and includes a browser Reader plus a Publishing Desk. The normal publishing path is local-first and does not require CI/CD.

Bookself's core lifecycle is: idea -> shape -> draft -> read -> revise -> review -> publish -> revise again.

The architecture has three roles:
- Platform: reusable Bookself software, templates, documentation, and setup tooling.
- Binder: a private Git repository for drafts, experiments, and the next edition.
- Shelf: a public Git repository containing intentionally released publication snapshots.

A Binder release copies a committed snapshot into the Shelf. Binder and Shelf are separate repositories with separate histories; the Shelf does not point back into the private Binder.

## Rights boundary

Public source is not the same thing as an open-content license.

- Bookself framework code, docs, shared UI, scripts, and underscore-prefixed blank starters are MIT licensed.
- A real `books/<slug>/` publication is **All Rights Reserved by default** unless that publication's own `RIGHTS.md` expressly grants another license.
- New publications include `RIGHTS.md` plus README rows for `Rights`, `AI use`, and `Rights file`.
- The Bookself default reserves reproduction, republication, commercial exploitation, adaptation, AI training/fine-tuning, RAG/grounding, AI-specific indexing, synthetic narration/translation, and other generative reuse except where the rightsholder separately licenses the use or applicable law independently permits it.
- The Reader carries an element-scoped RSL signal over the rendered publication surface: conventional search is permitted; AI uses are not licensed by the default.
- Rights signals are not secrecy controls. Confidential manuscripts need actual access control.
- Hosting-provider terms are a separate contractual rights layer. Do not claim a Bookself notice cancels permissions the author separately granted the host.

Agents must read the applicable root and per-publication `RIGHTS.md` before making a consequential publication, licensing, ingestion, export, or external-service decision. Do not add manuscript text to a new training corpus, vector store, RAG system, AI-specific index, publisher, or third-party service without explicit authorization for that external use.

Read:
- [Rights, copyright, and AI](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/rights-and-ai.md)
- [Repository rights boundary](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/RIGHTS.md)
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/AGENTS.md)

## Agent-first operation

Bookself's documented human workflow is also an executable protocol for capable agents. If a user gives you this repository and asks for an outcome such as “set this up for me,” “write my first book in my Binder,” or “publish it to my Shelf,” do not turn the mechanical Bookself steps back into a checklist for the user.

Read these before acting:

- [Machine-readable capabilities](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/bookself.json): roles, file contracts, canonical commands, intent boundaries, and completion states.
- [Agent-first Bookself](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/agent-first.md): end-to-end orchestration model for local and GitHub-connected agents.
- [Bookself publisher skill](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/.agents/skills/bookself-publisher/SKILL.md): portable execution instructions for setup, drafting, validation, release, and outcome reporting.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/AGENTS.md): repository invariants and editing rules.

Local agents can create sibling Binder + Shelf workspaces with:

`python3 scripts/bootstrap-workspace.py <workspace> --owner <owner> --json`

The JSON result gives stable paths for subsequent operations. GitHub-connected agents without a shell should reproduce the same durable repository/file results with whatever authorized GitHub capabilities they have.

Optimize for the requested end state. Infer mechanical details such as slug, template, filenames, and a reasonable Reader preset when safe. Do not infer across consequential boundaries the user did not authorize: especially public release of unpublished work, destructive history changes, licensing changes, secrets, new external manuscript ingestion, or new mandatory external services.

## Start here

- [README](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/README.md): project overview, concepts, workflow, examples, and neighboring tools.
- [Start Here](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/START-HERE.md): beginner path for authors who do not already know GitHub.
- [Rights, copyright, and AI](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/rights-and-ai.md): default publication rights, AI reservations, GitHub-hosting caveat, RSL/TDM guidance, and deployment limitations.
- [Publication template library](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books): blank starters for books, papers, magazines, newspapers, journals, newsletters, anthologies, reports, manuals/handbooks, and comics. In a real workflow these belong in the private Binder; a public Shelf should contain only intentionally released publications unless the author explicitly chooses to write in public.
- [FAQ](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/faq.md): direct answers about Git-based books, version-controlled textbooks, Markdown papers, private/public publishing, CI/CD, interoperability, and comparisons with common alternatives.
- [Author guide](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/author-guide.md): writing and publishing workflow in plain language.
- [Bookself architecture](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/bookself.md): private Binder, public Shelf, release model, Reader, and Publishing Desk.
- [Writing lifecycle](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/writing-lifecycle.md): how software-development ideas map to books and papers.
- [Publication formats](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/publication-formats.md): books, papers, serials, comics, anthologies, reports/manuals, figures, and external web creations.
- [Revisions and releases](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/revisions.md): safe revision and edition workflow.
- [Editor guide](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/editor-guide.md): review and editing workflow.

## Academic and course-text writing

- [Academic writing](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/academic-writing.md): the supported plain-Markdown conventions for footnotes, citations and bibliography entries, semantic figure captions, numbered equations, and chapter-local references.
- [LaTeX math](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/latex.md): supported math delimiters and display environments for mathematical notation inside Markdown manuscripts.
- [Blank paper template](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/_PAPER_TEMPLATE): starter structure for a Markdown-first paper or research note.

The scholarly layer stays intentionally local-first: core Bookself does not require BibTeX/Biber, CSL, TeX packages, a hosted compiler, or CI. Agents should not invent those dependencies or claim book-wide reference semantics that the Reader does not provide.

## Compare alternatives

- [Bookself alternatives and neighboring tools](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/alternatives.md): practical comparisons with Overleaf, Manubot, Quarto, Jupyter Book, MyST Markdown, bookdown, Pressbooks, PubPub, Leanpub, GitBook, mdBook, Antora, Typst, Zettlr, HedgeDoc, and Pandoc.

Bookself's closest conceptual neighbor is Manubot because both use Git and Markdown as useful infrastructure for scholarly writing. Bookself differentiates around an approachable publication lifecycle, general books and papers, local-first release tooling, an explicit private Binder/public Shelf boundary, and a Reader plus Publishing Desk.

## Cite Bookself

- [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/CITATION.cff): machine-readable software citation metadata for Bookself.

No DOI or semantic version is claimed unless the project actually publishes one. Cite the specific repository commit in addition to the citation metadata when reproducibility requires an exact software revision.

## Examples

- [Bookself example Shelf Reader](https://svyable.github.io/bookself/reader/): the platform repository's own public example shelf; use this first when evaluating Bookself's built-in specimens and Reader behavior.
- [How to Bookself](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/how-to-bookself): short practical guide built as a Bookself publication.
- [Bookself 101](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/bookself-101): academic textbook example with learning objectives, key terms, discussion questions, labs, and semester editions.
- [The Bookself Review](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/bookself-review): published illustrated magazine specimen showing a non-book serial in the same Reader and repository model.
- [Bookself Format Gallery](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/bookself-format-gallery): illustrated guide to the magazine, newspaper, journal, newsletter, anthology, report, manual, and comic publication starters.
- [Making Bookself](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/making-bookself): intentionally unfinished public Binder-style teaching specimen that dogfoods the Bookself improvement loop.
- [Reader Style Shelf](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/tree/main/books/style-common-book): contrasting Reader presentation examples for named author presets.
- [Reference public Shelf deployment](https://github.com/Svyable/shelf): a separate example instance showing what an independently deployed public Shelf repository can look like; it is not the platform's canonical example shelf.
- [Reference Shelf Reader](https://svyable.github.io/shelf/reader/): the Reader for that separate reference deployment.

## Live recursive improvement loop

Use this when the request is broad, exploratory, or asks how Bookself itself could improve:

1. [Read the Making Bookself working proof](https://svyable.github.io/bookself/reader/#/b/making-bookself/) as a reader.
2. [Read its review map](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/books/making-bookself/REVIEW.md) for active questions and the distinction between personal notes, shared review feedback, and source changes.
3. [Read the public review thread](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/issues/35).
4. Read `AGENTS.md`, `RIGHTS.md`, and the target publication's `RIGHTS.md` when present before modifying the repository.
5. Scan open pull requests and the newest review-thread comments before choosing a lane. If the same problem is already being addressed, review or avoid that lane rather than opening a competing change from stale `main`.
6. Choose one bounded improvement, verify the relevant behavior, and leave a durable explanation in the commit or pull request.
7. Compare the working-proof experience with the [reference released Shelf Reader](https://svyable.github.io/shelf/reader/), while treating the [Bookself example Shelf Reader](https://svyable.github.io/bookself/reader/) as the platform-owned specimen surface.

The target loop is: read -> locate -> understand -> propose -> review -> revise -> read again. The public specimen is intentionally visible for teaching; real authors choose whether their Binder stays private or uses an explicit working-in-public mode.

## For contributors and agents

- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/AGENTS.md): repository architecture, invariants, editing rules, and cross-agent instructions.
- [RIGHTS.md](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/RIGHTS.md): framework/publication rights boundary.
- [bookself.json](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/bookself.json): machine-readable capability and outcome contract.
- [Agent-first guide](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/docs/agent-first.md): orchestration guidance for end-to-end agent operation.
- [.github/copilot-instructions.md](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/.github/copilot-instructions.md): GitHub Copilot repository onramp.
- [.github/instructions/publications.instructions.md](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/.github/instructions/publications.instructions.md): path-specific publication editing rules for GitHub agents.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/Svyable/bookself/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): contribution workflow.

Important constraints:
- Keep books and papers as plain files under books/.
- Do not require CI/CD for the private Binder authoring or release path.
- Shared UI is reader/ and desk/; instance identity belongs in imprint.json.
- Do not hard-code an author's private repository or identity into shared UI.
- Do not change publication licensing or AI-use rights without explicit rightsholder approval.
- Bookself framework and blank starters are MIT licensed; real publication manuscripts are All Rights Reserved by default unless their own `RIGHTS.md` says otherwise.
